Table card with a year or indicator control

Source: R/chart-table_downloads.R
cd_table_ui.Rd

A card that shows a data frame as a table, with a control above it (a year chip or an indicator chip) and a download of the data as an Excel workbook in the card's header. The module translates the column headings it knows, rounds the numbers and aligns them. Use it for the table that goes with a page's charts. For a formatted table (a flextable), use cd_table_card_ui().

Usage

cd_table_ui(
  id,
  i18n,
  title_key,
  control_type = c("year", "indicator"),
  width = 6
)

cd_table_server(
  id,
  cache,
  i18n,
  data,
  columns = NULL,
  control_type = c("year", "indicator"),
  filename = reactive("download"),
  label_key = "btn_global_download_data",
  extension = reactive("xlsx"),
  data_transform = NULL,
  excel_write_fun = NULL,
  excel_sheet = NULL,
  excel_title = NULL,
  about = NULL
)

Arguments

id

The module's id.

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

title_key

The translation key of the card's title.

control_type

The control above the table: "year" (the default) or "indicator".

width

The card's width, passed to the kit's cd_table_card(). Default 6. The kit's card takes a width and ignores it: a card is as wide as the place it is put in.

cache

A reactive that returns the dataset, a CacheConnection.

data

A reactive that returns the data frame the table shows.

columns

A named list of reactable::colDef(), named by column. Each one replaces or adds to what the module sets for that column (heading, cell, alignment). Entries for columns the data does not have are dropped. NULL (the default) changes nothing.

filename

A reactive that returns the first part of the downloaded file's name. Default reactive("download").

label_key

The translation key of the download button's label. Default "btn_global_download_data".

extension

A reactive that returns the downloaded file's extension. Default reactive("xlsx"). The file is an Excel workbook whatever the extension says.

data_transform

A function function(data) applied to data() before the table is drawn, for example to choose or rename columns. NULL (the default) shows data() as it is.

excel_write_fun

A function function(wb, data) that writes data() into the openxlsx workbook wb, adding the sheets it needs. NULL (the default) uses excel_sheet, or the plain download described in Details.

excel_sheet

The translation key of the sheet's name, for a download that holds data() on one sheet. Used only when excel_write_fun is NULL. Default NULL.

excel_title

The translation key of a title written above the data on that sheet. Used only with excel_sheet. Default NULL, no title.

about

What the table is, for the app's AI: NULL (the default), a list, or a function that returns a list. See datasuite.ui::ai_register_component().

Value

cd_table_ui() returns the UI as Shiny tags (the card).

cd_table_server() returns a reactive holding the control's value: the chosen year as a string, or the chosen indicator's code.

Details

The control. Give control_type the same value in the ui and the server call.

  • "year": a chip listing the dataset's years (cache()$data_years), which starts on the first of them. When the data has a year column, the table shows only the rows of the chosen year.

  • "indicator": an indicator chip (cd_indicator_ui()) offering every indicator. The module does not filter by it. The page reads the chosen indicator from the reactive the server returns and builds data from it.

The columns. These headings are translated without the page doing anything: year, adminlevel_1, district and month; columns whose name starts with cov_ (coverage); columns whose name ends with _med or _mad (median and MAD of an indicator) and the indicator's own column beside them; and, with the indicator control, the column named after the chosen indicator. Every other column keeps its name unless columns gives it a heading. Numbers are shown rounded to whole numbers and aligned to the right, except year and month.

The download. The file is an Excel workbook named filename(), then the control's value, then the date and time. What it holds depends on the arguments:

  • With excel_write_fun, that function writes the workbook from data().

  • Else with excel_sheet, data() is written on one sheet with that name, under excel_title when it is given.

  • With neither, the data the table is drawn from (data() after data_transform) is written on one sheet named "Data".

With a year control the download holds the year the control is on, as the table does and as the file's name says.

The table is also registered with the app's AI bridge, which can then list it and read its data.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# in a page's ui
cd_table_ui(ns("rates"), i18n, "title_rr_main", control_type = "year")

# in the page's server
year <- cd_table_server("rates", cache, i18n,
  data = reactive(my_rates(cache())),
  columns = list(anc_rr = reactable::colDef(name = "ANC", cell = cd_rate_status_cell)),
  filename = reactive("reporting_rate"),
  excel_sheet = "title_rr_main"
)
} # }
